diagnosis: Entry flow under v5 is clean. All 8 booked invoices (51, 52, 54-58, 60) ran the same 15 steps with 0 wasted: lower 'Supplier' -> type_supplier (+Return) -> date line -> type_date -> '+ Add Row' -> '× Item' -> type_item (+Return) -> '$0.00' below Rate -> type_amount -> Save -> Yes -> Submit -> Yes. Keep the enter logic as it is.

The only failure, invoice 59 (Pinecone), is a read error, not an entry error. Jev picked the total line '$49.87' (confidence 0.48, read_ok amount=False), entered it correctly and submitted it as PINV-1008 with the wrong amount.

Likely cause is my v5 wording 'Pick the SHORTEST line that is just an amount'. On an invoice with several bare amounts (line item, subtotal), that wording favours a line-item figure. The v4 hint recorded a Pinecone line '$50.00 USD due May 1, 2026', and invoice 59 is Pinecone dated May 1, 2026, so the true total is almost certainly $50.00 and $49.87 is a line item or subtotal.

The 'due <date>' line is dangerous to pick because the year gets parsed as the amount. But the amount inside it is the true total. Jev should use it as a cross-check and pick the other line that shows the same amount.
Invoice 53 (WellyBox, ILS) was handled with 0 steps and success=True. The currency read is correct, so nothing changes there.

Speed: two decisions were identical in 8 of 8 runs and carry no real choice. After type_date Jev always clicked '+ Add Row' (641,473; conf 0.95-0.97). After type_amount Jev always clicked 'Save' (1302,67; conf 0.79-0.91). Each costs one Jev call plus settle time and can be a reflex.
Every screen captured after an action was fully drawn at the current settle times (S7, S12, S14 and similar). That leaves room for a small reduction.

changes.why: The 'shortest bare amount' rule made Jev pick $49.87 on the Pinecone invoice when the amount due was different.
changes.evidence: invoice 59: total line '$49.87', conf 0.48, amount read_ok=False; v4 hint cites Pinecone '$50.00 USD due May 1, 2026'
